feedback.problem:
The Sun has a mass of $(1.99\times {10}^{30})\,\text{kg}$ and Neptune has a mass of $(1.02\times {10}^{26})\,\text{kg}.$ The magnitude of the gravitational force between them is $(6.69\times {10}^{20})\,\text{N}.$ According to Newton's law of universal gravitation, what is the distance between the centers of mass of the Sun and Neptune? Write your answer in scientific notation, rounding to **three significant figures** where appropriate. Assume the Newtonian constant of gravitation is $G=(6.67\times {10}^{-11})\,{\text{m}}^{3}/(\text{kg}\cdot {\text{s}}^{2}).$

The distance between the Sun and Neptune is
$(${{field-1}}
$\times $
{{field-2}}$)\,\text{m}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Newton's law of universal gravitation states that the gravitational force attracting two objects is proportional to the product of the two masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers of mass:

$$
F=G\frac{{m}_{1}{m}_{2}}{{r}^{2}}
$$

where

- $F$ is the gravitational force between the objects, measured in Newtons $(\text{N}),$

- $G=(6.67\times {10}^{-11})\,{\text{m}}^{3}/(\text{kg}\cdot {\text{s}}^{2})$ is the Newtonian constant of gravitation,

- ${m}_{1}$ and ${m}_{2}$ are the masses of the objects, measured in $\text{kg},$ and

- $r$ is the distance between their centers of mass, measured in $\text{m}.$

First, let's rearrange the formula to make $r$ the subject:

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =G\frac{{m}_{1}{m}_{2}}{{r}^{2}} \\ {r}^{2} & =G\frac{{m}_{1}{m}_{2}}{F} \\ r & =\sqrt{G\frac{{m}_{1}{m}_{2}}{F}}\end{aligned}
$$

Let ${m}_{1}$ be the mass of the Sun and ${m}_{2}$ be the mass of Neptune. Then, substituting in the known values, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{2} & =(6.67\times {10}^{-11})\cdot \frac{(1.99\times {10}^{30})\cdot (1.02\times {10}^{26})}{6.69\times {10}^{20}} \\  & =\frac{6.67\cdot 1.99\cdot 1.02}{6.69}\times \frac{{10}^{-11}\cdot {10}^{30}\cdot {10}^{26}}{{10}^{20}} \\  & =(2.0237…)\times {10}^{25} \\  & =(20.237…)\times {10}^{24}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, taking the square root, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{20.237…\times {10}^{24}} \\  & =\sqrt{20.237…}\times \sqrt{{10}^{24}} \\  & =(4.498…)\times {10}^{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, rounded to three significant figures, the distance between the Sun and Neptune is
$(\,4.50\times {10}^{12}\,)\,\text{m}.$
